question: What fish evidence does the 2003 WWF-Philippines Sulu-Sulawesi assessment report for Ragay Gulf, and can the aggregate be resolved to species or sanctuary sites?
purpose: Review a historical Ragay Gulf fish-visual-census summary and its cited protected-area context. This is not a current fish inventory, sanctuary-status verification, legal-boundary review, or complete reef checklist.
searchMethod: Retrieved the complete 278-page report from a university-hosted third-party mirror on 2026-11-01 and reviewed printed pages 119-120, the references at printed page 217, and Appendix 5 at printed page 271. Checked the PDF front matter for authorship, date, publisher, and rights language. This is a bounded review of the identified report, not an exhaustive search of the underlying historical survey archive.

bibliography.citation: Alcala, A., Alava, M., Anglo, E., Aragones, N., Bate, E., Guarin, F., Hermes, R., Lagunzad, D., Montebon, A. R., Miclat, R., Palma, J. A., Pe-Montebon, J., Nacorda, H. M., Perez, T., Trono, G., Jr., & Yaptinchay, A. A. (2003, May). A Biophysical Assessment of the Philippine Territory of the Sulu-Sulawesi Marine Ecoregion. Sulu-Sulawesi Marine Ecoregion Program, WWF-Philippines.
reportPagesReviewed: printed pages 119-120: reef fish summaries for Southern Luzon and Ragay Gulf
printed page 217: selected bibliography entry for MPDITF-NRMC 1982
printed page 271: Appendix 5, Marine Protected Areas in the Philippines

findings.ragayGulfAggregate: The report describes Ragay Gulf as in Quezon and Camarines Sur, names Alibijaban and Acha Reef as fish sanctuaries, and states that a fish visual census resulted in 296 species under 18 families. It identifies Labridae, Caesionidae, Pomacentridae, and Chaetodontidae as dominant families.
findings.resolutionLimits: The report supplies no scientific-species checklist, survey date, station list, effort, vouchers, or allocation of records between Alibijaban, Acha Reef, and any other Ragay Gulf site. The paragraph does not identify a supporting bibliography citation for the 296-species statement. Its placement after the sanctuary names does not establish that all observations came from those two sanctuaries.
findings.appendixContext: Appendix 5 lists Acha Reef Fish Sanctuary and Alibijaban Island Mangrove Wilderness Area and Marine Protected Area with brief protection-purpose text. This is historical report wording only; it does not verify current legal designation, boundaries, restrictions, or enforceability.
findings.separateBalayanCitationIssue: The immediately preceding Balayan Bay paragraph reports 329 reef-fish species and cites MPDITF-NRMC 1982. The report bibliography identifies that 1982 item as Sombrero Island Marine Park, a separate Batangas locality. This leaves the Balayan citation-to-locality crosswalk unresolved; it is not evidence about Ragay Gulf and is not used to qualify the separate 296-species claim.
findings.geographicScope: The report presents the fish summary at Ragay Gulf scale, across its stated Quezon and Camarines Sur setting. It does not support assignment to the Quezon side, any particular municipality, the Guinayangan sanctuary, a named reef, or a present-day waterbody polygon.

accessAndRights.access: The full PDF was reviewed online at a university-hosted third-party mirror. The front matter identifies WWF-Philippines and credits WWF-US funding; this host was not treated as the publisher or rights holder.
accessAndRights.reuse: No item-specific open license or permission statement was identified in the reviewed PDF. Retain citation and short factual research notes only; do not reproduce the report's text, tables, figures, or any unverified underlying species list in the public app.
accessAndRights.rawRetention: No PDF copy or extracted table was added to the repository.

decision.reason: The source supports only an old, gulf-level aggregate and family context. It does not expose taxa, survey stations/dates, sanctuary allocation, current legal status, or item-specific reuse terms.

nextAction: Keep the 296-species statement as historical gulf-level discovery context. Prioritize retrieval of the original visual-census report or a rights-cleared, station-resolved checklist before considering species rows. Keep the Balayan Bay 329-species reference issue separate from Ragay Gulf.

sources.supports: Report title, credits and date; Ragay Gulf 296-species/18-family summary; historical MPA labels in Appendix 5; and the separate Balayan Bay 329-species paragraph and its bibliography entry.
